commit: 834d8ec1 on branch save-speed (/home/user/work/save-speed, base e13dce3d). Release build without new warnings, clang-format applied.
before: v13 base, song with 3 of 8 synths (about 50% CPU), saving from bar 2 (chord change): 344 ms emulated. Of this, 338.6 ms go to AudioEngine::routine(), 5.3 ms to generating the XML, 0.11 ms to UI/OLED/PIC, 0.03 ms to cluster loading and 0.004 ms to FatFS. There are 310 routine() calls (about one every 5 samples, with the render time subtracted) with 618 windows of around 24 samples (P5 to P95: 20 to 28). Biggest gap: 80 samples. With 5 synths (about 70% CPU) it takes 716 ms, and the biggest gap is 128 samples (1 sample underrun). Mid-bar: 80 ms and 180 ms respectively.
after: 3 synths: 21.8 ms instead of 344 ms (about 16 times faster). Of this, audio 16.8 ms, XML 5.0 ms, 30 calls (16 of them render), windows 61 samples on average, biggest gap 71. 5 synths: 65.7 ms instead of 716 ms, biggest gap 97, no underrun. Mid-bar: 10.3 ms and 16.0 ms, gaps 56 and 66. In no case did the DMA play old buffer data (checked sample by sample). The written XML is identical (sha256). Normal playback stays bit-exactly the same.
change: New function routineWhileAccessingFile() in storage_manager.cpp, called from XMLSerializer::write() and XMLDeserializer::xmlReadDone(). It serves audio and UI only when at least 8 samples are due; checking this only reads the DMA position. Then routine() renders at least 64 samples ahead (AudioEngine::minNumSamplesToRender, set only during the file access), and the following calls only output. A plain threshold of 32 would also have been faster, but made the gap with 5 synths worse, at 138.
risks: The SD card's wait time is not modeled in the emulator (while waiting, the task manager takes over, unchanged). Loading during playback was not measured directly, only the same call density when loading (median every 3.3 samples). Songs above 100% CPU (6 to 8 synths without culling) have underruns with and without the change, to the same degree. A test on the device is still pending.

reproduced:
I measured both ELFs myself with SAVE=1 (base deluge-base.elf, where according to the nm diff only the expected functions differ, and save-speed 834d8ec1). The numbers match exactly: 344→21.8 ms, 716→65.7 ms, 80→10.3 ms and 180→16.0 ms. The biggest gap is 80→71, 128 (underrun)→97, 50→56 and 53→66 samples. The XML is the same in both builds (sha256).

I newly measured the harder cases:
- 4 synths: 568→44 ms, gap 104→82.
- 6 synths: both builds run into underruns (5936 and 5808 underrun samples respectively, 1012→823 ms).
- Emulated CPU at 280 instead of 400 MHz (equivalent to an IPC of about 0.7): with 3 synths from bar 2 both run into underruns (601 and 469 underrun samples respectively). With 5 synths mid-bar: 577→55 ms, gap 117→96.

So the new version never has an underrun where the base has none. Under light load the gap is somewhat bigger (up to 66), but stays far below 128. According to the analysis: gap ≤ 8 + check interval + render time for 64 samples. That stays below 128 as long as the base itself has no underrun.

The following is not critical:
- The SD wait times (yield and routineForSD with minNumSamplesToRender=0) are unchanged.
- The RX input is 128 to 256 samples behind, so rendering ahead is covered.
- The DMA position is already valid before the first XML read (ssiInit before readSettingsFromFile).
- UI/OLED/PIC still run at least every 8 samples. Buttons and MIDI input were not served here before either.
- No new warnings, clang-format is applied.

Not measured: loading during playback.

problems.problem: When saving or loading, MIDI clock out and trigger clock out can be sent 128 samples (2.9 ms) too early. This comes from rendering 64 samples ahead.
problems.where: audio_engine.cpp scheduleMidiGateOutISR(): samplesTilMIDIOrGate = (t - movement - due) & 127, together with minNumSamplesToRender=64
problems.evidence: The analysis rests on measured values, not on a MIDI test. A sample at window position t is played 128 - due + t samples after the render start. At t ≥ due + render time, & 127 cuts off exactly 128 samples, so the timer fires 2.9 ms too early. Measured with 3 synths mid-bar: due about 8, rendering 64 samples takes about 29 samples. So clock ticks at t = 37 to 63, i.e. around 40% of the clock pulses during saving or loading, land too early. In the base (windows of about 24, due about 15) this practically does not happen.
problems.fix: Compute the delay without wrapping: s = t + SSI_TX_BUFFER_NUM_SAMPLES - due - (movement & 127). Keep the old behavior only when s ≤ 0. The timer is sufficient for this (≤ 255 × 11.7 counts). Alternatively, set the minimum window only when no MIDI or trigger clock tick is scheduled.
